This week, Dex turns two. Great timing to humblebrag about our Q4, but I wouldn't. Instead, I'd share the struggles of building a non-census company as a group of parents. A few days ago, Charlie and I had a co-founder heart-to-heart. I walked him to BART, and he was shaking in the SF wind. “Why?” I asked. “Last week the whole family was sick, right when we’re fast-following the subscription launch. That week really got me,” Charlie replied, and sighed. All of a sudden, guilt took over. His wife told me—half-jokingly—that Charlie wakes up every day at 3:30AM and sneaks out like a thief into the home office. Sometimes their daughter wakes up and asks, “What time is it, Dad? Where are you going?” Charlie slips away as if he didn’t hear. I laughed and lightheartedly told Charlie to take it easy. But I felt guilty. Our lives run like clockwork: wake up, work, parenting, work, parenting, sleep. 7 days a week. 52 weeks a year. Every kid’s sick day is a major boss fight. Every weekend feels like a juggling act because we can’t unplug from work or parenting. And as the CEO, I felt bad. Dex is a hard business, and I sorta got everyone (mostly parents themselves) into this mission impossible. Think about it… we’re trying to create the canonical children’s technology—AI, software, content, devices, EVERYTHING—by a team of 8 FTE in a sardine office, with $5M in funding. Every hour matters. Every dollar matters. We want scale. We also want profitability. We want speed. We also want quality. In Q4, we magically got all of those. Then I realized: we also want each employee to be happy, and their families well taken care of. How can I have it all, continuously? Fundraising and hiring? Deep down, I know Dex is an underdog company. We need to achieve so much to convince the “mainstream”/“playbooked” investors. So I don't want to waste time until we're undeniably exceptional. Be less ambitious? I consider Dex the work of my life. I’d rather reach for the vision and fail than not try. Parent less? No way. Unfair for our children. Unfair for our better halves. So the truth is, I don’t know how to have it all. What I do know is: tomorrow, I’ll live to fight another day—to defend our vision, take care of the team, and be a good parent. Gladly, those struggles come with a bright side. When I’m stretched thin, I think about my Ironman races. In the last leg, each step felt like hell. But each step also gave me that rush: I’m reaching a point I’ve never reached before. Building Dex is like racing an Ironman, but with a mission. Each day of relentless work is a testament to our vision. Just like every early morning, late night, and weekend of showing up to our children is a testament to our love for them. If you made this far: thank you. This was personal. I hope it gives you a little energy, too. ...more ...more

We’re excited to announce Raindrop 's $15M seed round led by Lightspeed . We’re lucky to be trusted by some of the fastest growing AI companies including Replit , Speak , Clay , Framer , Portola , Avoca , and AngelList to help them monitor their AI agents. In the last two years, the world has gone from simple chatbots to agents that can use thousands of tools and run for hours. Traditional AI tests, or evals, were designed for the chatbot era. They don’t measure agent performance in the real-world. Raindrop is the monitoring platform for AI Agents. We’ve built: • the first automatic issue detection system for detecting silent agent failures • the most powerful way to search AI production data • the first Agent-native A/B testing platform We’ve shipped a lot. but our job certainly isn’t done yet. Our vision is to build the first true flywheel for continuous agent improvement. We’re building a world class team to help us complete the mission, and hiring engineers across ML, Infra, and Product. DM me or apply at the link in the comments :) ...more ...more

Today I’m debuting Parable: https://parablevc.com/ Thank you to everyone for your support that resulted in an oversubscribed Fund I from world class endowments and institutions. Successful companies make the impossible, inevitable. Their stories live long enough to become parables that inspire generations. We write up to $10M checks to founders progressing humanity. You create the category, and we go all in to help you lead it. Parable has led five rounds, and is actively investing in pre-seed, seed, and series A’s with a focus on Consumer and Prosumer AI. We love co-leading and leading. We are also happy to be creative in partnering with founders we believe in. Ideas precede invention, and ideologies govern Silicon Valley. Here’s what I believe: I. We are in extraordinary times. Many of us have grand ambitions to build generational companies. These extra-ordinary times favor the “ordinary mind”: a Chinese concept written as “平常心” and translated literally as “usual heart”. It is the mentality of the humble everyday. It leads to persistence and to clear thinking; dominant daily practices of startup journeys that endure (an idea attributed to Bytedance founder Zhang Yiming). II. We live in a new world. Humanity itself is evolving. AI is a new archetype of “person”. The upside case: we add infinitely more “people”, ostensibly a new type of population growth, with many “persons” designed by and for each of us. It could be the best friend you’ve ever had…you can vent infinitely without upsetting them! It could be the best colleague you’ve ever worked with…you can offload anything or everything. These “people” have narrow superpowers and in their superpowers they are potentially better than even the best of us. This transforms how we live life and how we work. III. We do outstanding work when we pursue our life’s work. I aspire to partner with as many great founders doing great work as possible. Founders who solve problems that appear small at the outset, but over time become important global phenomena. This is my life’s work. We’re hiring. We’re actively investing. If you’ve made it this far, don’t be shy and say hello: anne [at] parablevc [.] com! ...more ...more

Excited to be a launch partner for Baseten Labs! We believe that the future is multi-model (and multi-modal). That's why we're partnering with Baseten to bring agentic search to every dataset. People often misinterpret "The Bitter Lesson": It's about using general methods, not about creating general models. AlphaGo (it's prime example) is the opposite of general (it only plays Go) but was trained using general methods. There is value to general models, but often this generality comes at the cost of outright performance. So what you really want to maximize is leverage on computation. At SID.ai , we have found ways to get much more leverage for the task of search. We expect many other tasks to go this way. The future will be multi-model not as a compromise to save money, but because specialized models are simply better: faster, cheaper, and more accurate at the thing you actually need. Unlike Go, search is very useful. We’re thrilled to partner with Baseten to bring this utility to everyone. Together we offer agentic search at 20x lower latency and 100x lower cost than a general frontier model, at equal or better accuracy. As always: reach out if you want to chat & we're hiring!

This past week, I had the opportunity to attend Jane Street 's WiSE program in NYC and Y Combinator 's Startup School 2026 in SF. At WiSE, I loved getting an inside look at the world of quantitative finance through panels, conversations with Jane Streeters, and playing mock trading games. I met so many girls who share my interests in math and CS - huge thank you to Katie Nasta and Kylie Newman for organizing such a engaging program! At YC Startup School, among all the spontaneous conversations I had, a few highlights included attending the Future Female Founders Summit, speaking with David S. Roberts about the AI/Biotech space and multimodal fusion during a breakout session, and learning from Gabriel Birnbaum about his work in AI-based storytelling during the career fair. As Sam Altman said, the best ideas start with believing in a possibility long before everyone else sees it. What an unforgettable week!

Thank you WIRED magazine for naming Dex as one of your "Favorite Brain-Boosting Toys for Kids of All Ages." We love that our language discovery camera makes it fun and easy for kids to explore languages (16 languages and 30+ dialects). All they have to do is point and click and Dex will identify the word in their chosen language. But it's much more than a camera, as Wired put it, "it can turn pictures into flash cards and use spoken stories to, you know, make learning fun." https://lnkd.in/dCuZ4CmY

At Dex , we’re always looking for playful ways to help kids remember what they discover. 🔎 Something that’ll stick in their memory, without feeling like a task. Meet Dex Stickers - a new and fun way for kids to explore, collect and grow. All they have to do is take a photo 🤳 and Dex will identify the object and present a black & white sticker of what they snapped. Each sticker will be filled with color 🎨 as they delve into the topic further. Dex will also provide bite-sized facts for kids to help them understand how or what the object is used for. Dex Stickers offer endless opportunities for children to create and collect. What do think your child's first sticker will be?

Two years ago, I joined DramaBox to build something that didn't exist yet: a US content production studio for vertical short drama, from the ground up. Today, I'm closing that chapter, and I'm carrying so much with me. We built a team from scratch and a methodology that connected development, production, and market strategy into one loop. When I arrived, content and growth barely spoke to each other. By the end, every project was a full-cycle conversation between them. We produced at a scale and hit rate I'm deeply proud of. We spearheaded our Disney Accelerator journey and the partnership that grew from it. And we went beyond making shows, partnering with Cal State LA to teach the next generation of filmmakers how to make microdrama, and helping build the creative ecosystem this format needs to last. But the thing I'll carry most is the people. This team trusted me, built alongside me, and cared about the work in a way that made all of it possible. Thank you. I'll be cheering you on always. So, what's next? I'm thrilled to share that I've joined Pocket FM as AVP, Head of Content. Here's the bet I'm making. I believe the next year in this industry belongs to retention. The last few years were about acquisition, everyone competing to pull users in. But as that gets more expensive and attention more fragmented, the winners will be the ones who can actually keep people. And that comes down to one thing: content worth coming back to. I also think AI is about to change the shape of storytelling in a way most people aren't expecting. As production cost collapses, the constraint on length disappears, and I believe content trends longer, deeper, and more immersive, not shorter. Pocket FM has been building exactly that in audio: stories people return to for hundreds of hours. That's a future I want to help shape. New medium, new challenge. I'm here to learn, and I'm here to build. If you're working on the future of content, AI storytelling, or audio, let's connect.
